meta.method: lds-harvest-auto.mjs run 2wzwz: resources chosen by the written rules; every row of every sheet or CSV read (CSV over 20 MB streamed and not stored; large xlsx streamed with ExcelJS); a row is kept when it is a zone row (harvest-log.json meta.rules.zone_row): zone OA/LSOA/MSOA/ward code, zone postcode or postcode sector, zone UPRN or TOID, or coordinates in the 3D model box. zone_keys gives the key that matched, row by row. header_rows: the rows above the first data row.
selection_notes: name keys: 50 zone station names (zone-names.json); a cell equal to one (normalised) is a zone row, a weaker key than a code

rows: Train Operator of westbound train 334 started-up against signal TL11 at danger by less than one car. The correct procedure was carried out and Train Operator was given authority to continue under rule. DMT established during interview that the Train Operator viewed the correct signal, but misread the aspect.

Train Operator of westbound train 317 passed signal TN200 at danger by 65 metres from front of the train at a speed between 10 and 18 mph. The correct procedure was carried out and Train Operator was given authority to continue under rule. Duty Manager Trains established during interview that the Train Operator failed to check the signal's aspect. He had become distracted by looking at DLR building works. Note TN200 is believed to be a poorly positioned signal due to sighting distance being reduced as a wall is obstructing the aspect.
Eastbound Central line train 77 passed signal LIS5063 at danger without prior authority whilst in ATO working.

Train Operator of westbound Train 56 passed approach speed control draw-up signal A8400 at Danger by less than one car. The Service Controller was informed and the Service Operator gave authority for the train to fully berth in the platform under rule. Arrangements were made for the Train Operator to be interviewed by Duty Manager Trains at Barking, who found that the T/Operator had observed the repeater signal correctly, but then expected A8400 to clear on approach.

Train Operator of westbound Train 205 started up against signal WK2 at Danger, upon departure from platform 7. He stated to Duty Manager Trains during interview that he had joined the train having stepped back from the previous train. He entered the cab, heard a noise and assumed the train stop had lowered. He overlooked to re-check the starting signal or Rear Cab Clear indication, and started the train forward about � a car. The tripcock operated and the train came to a stand. The Service Controller was informed and he was given authority to set the train back into the platform under the wrong direction movement (WDM) procedure. He was relieved from duty at Waterloo for a fact finding interview at 09:55 Hours. The T/Operator stated that he was on auto pilot as he entered the cab and assumed the noise he heard had been the train stop lower. He realised that this was not the case as the train came to a stand. He added that he knew that he should have checked the signal aspect as normal and could not explain why he had failed to do so. He added that his mind was elsewhere and not fully focused on the normal checks. He had slept badly overnight due to a noise disturbance.

Instructor Train Operator of westbound train 214 passed signal OE260 at danger by less than one car. The correct procedure was carried out and Instructor Train Operator was given authority to continue under rule. Duty Manager Trains established during interview that the Instructor Train Operator failed to check the signal's aspect due to momentary lapse of concentration (was thinking about what to do now he's moved house).

Train Operator of westbound train 121 passed draw-up signal A8400 at danger by less than one car. The correct procedure was carried out and Train Operator was given authority to continue under rule, after contacting the Cannon Street Station Supervisor and the Service Manager. Duty Manager Trains established during interview that the Train Operator failed to react correctly to a caution signal. He was aware of the aspect on the repeater R8400 displaying a caution aspect, but on entering Cannon Street platform due to the nature of the westbound working through the City area, the train was held at Monument and there was general slow moving, so lost concentration and did not react sufficiently to the danger aspect on signal A8400.

Westbound Hammersmith & City line train 216 was front tripped at signal OB45, after it was returned back to danger by Signal Operator in error, when he believed train 216 was at signal OB27. The Train Operator was subsequently authorised to set back the train back into the platform under the Wrong Direction Move procedure.

Train Operator of eastbound train 316 started up against signal TM3. The Train Operator was subsequently authorised to set back into the platform after neither the Train Operator or Station Staff were able to see the route secure indicator that would have allowed the train to proceed under rule.

Train Operator of eastbound Metropolitan line train 447 started-up against signal A249 at danger by less than one car. The correct procedure was carried out and Train Operator was given authority to continue under rule, after the Station Supervisor had been sent to the train by the Service Controller. Duty Manager Trains established during interview that the Train Operator failed to check the signal's aspect (failed to carry out the SODOS procedure correctly). It should be noted that he was having bad stomach pains at the time and had already visited the toilet on three occasions. He was contemplating his next toilet stop at the next station Aldgate and his attention was diverted.
Eastbound train 303 started up against signal TM3 at danger. The train was authorised to proceed under rule.

Train Operator of train 435 started-up against signal A249 at danger by less than one car. The correct procedure was carried out and Train Operator was given authority to continue under rule once Station Staff had attended and observed the Train Operator. Duty Manager Trains established during interview that the Train Operator failed to check the signal's aspect. After speaking with the Train Operator, he stated there was a major service disruption on the Circle, Hammersmith & City and District lines at the time of the SPaD. Liverpool Street was the last main interchange station for passengers to alight and re-plan their journey for a service disruption, bearing in mind Aldgate was the last stop on the Metropolitan line. Train Operator was making regular and continuous announcements advising passengers of the disruption. He noticed people were boarding then alighting after hearing his PAs. He also noticed people looking confused on the monitors, so made further PAs to again inform passengers of the service delay and their options. Once passengers were clear, he closed the train doors and wound up against the station starting signal A249 at danger.

Train Operator of westbound train 471 passed speed controller signal OE260 at danger by less than one car. The correct procedure was carried out and Train Operator was given authority to continue under rule. Duty Manager Trains established during interview that the Train Operator had been distracted by a person acting suspiciously on the platform. He has been reminded to have his train under control at all times.
Train Operator of southbound Northern line train 42 started up against signal X643 at danger without prior authority. The Train Operator was subsequently authorised to continue under rule.

Train Operator of westbound District line train 104 passed signal OB46 at danger by less than one car. The correct procedure was carried out and Train Operator was given authority to continue under rule, after he had contacted the Service Controller, who in turn contacted the Signal Operator. The Service Controller then contacted the Station Supervisor to attend and they confirmed Train Operator was fit to continue. It was established during interview that the Train Operator failed to react correctly to a caution signal. He was also thinking about his father's medical condition (currently in hospital). Train Operator is to always check signals correctly in future and not allow his mind to wonder. Although the Upminster Management Team are aware of his personal circumstances, it is his sole responsibility to keep management informed of any changes, especially if it will affect his driving performance.

Train Operator of westbound Metropolitan line train 420  passed draw-up signal OE260 at danger by less than one car. The correct procedure was carried out and Train Operator was given authority to continue under rule. It was established during interview that the Train Operator anticipated signal clearance. The Train Operator was reminded that he should never make assumptions that the signal will always clear like it has done in the past. To be aware that train movements ahead may cause the signal to remain at danger.

Train Operator of westbound Circle & Hammersmith line train 210 passed signal A8400 at danger by less than one car. The correct procedure was carried out and Train Operator was given authority to continue under rule. It was established during interview that the Train Operator failed to check the signal's aspect (failed to check and obey the yellow aspect on the repeater for signal A8400). He had become distracted by radio message and train on the eastbound platform applying the rule at station starter.

Train Operator of westbound Circle & Hammersmith line train 246 passed station starter signal EG2 at danger. It is believed he had been distracted from normal platform duties, because two charity collectors in hospital uniform were jumping in and out of the cars. Train Operator was advised to contact the Service Operator. The Service Operator requested the Train Operator remain where he was and await further instructions, while he liaised with the Service Controller. The Station Supervisor liaised with the Service Controller and Service Operator before posting a hand signal person at the extent of the move and filling out the Wrong Directional Movement form. The Station Supervisor handed the Wrong Directional Movement form to the Train Operator, who changed ends and completed the move. Once the train was berthed back into the platform, the Train Operator changed ends and departed under clear signals.

Train Operator of Outer Rail Circle line Train 231 started-up against signal EG2 at danger. The correct procedure was carried out and the Train Operator was given authority to set back into the platform using the Wrong Direction Movement procedure. It was established during interview that the Train Operator viewed the wrong signal (read through).
